title: NovaCorp Employee Code of Conduct
content:
NovaCorp Employee Code of Conduct — Revised August 2025

1. PURPOSE
This Code of Conduct sets the standard of behavior expected of all NovaCorp employees, contractors, and representatives. Adherence to this code is a condition of continued employment.

2. PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT
All employees must treat colleagues, clients, and partners with respect and professionalism. Discrimination, harassment, or bullying on the basis of race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination.

3. ANTI-HARASSMENT POLICY
Harassment includes unwanted verbal, physical, or visual conduct of a sexual nature, hostile work environment, quid pro quo arrangements, and cyberbullying. All employees have a duty to report harassment. Reports may be made directly to HR, through the anonymous Ethics Hotline (1-800-555-NOVA), or to any senior manager.

4. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST
Employees must avoid situations where personal interests conflict with NovaCorp's interests. This includes accepting gifts valued over $50, engaging in outside employment with a competitor, or making business decisions that benefit a family member. All potential conflicts must be disclosed to HR.

5. CONFIDENTIALITY
Employees must protect NovaCorp's confidential information, including trade secrets, customer data, financial information, and personnel records. Confidentiality obligations survive employment termination.

6. ACCEPTABLE USE OF COMPANY RESOURCES
Company resources — including computers, email, and networks — are for business use. Incidental personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with work, consume significant resources, or involve illegal or inappropriate content.

7. DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
Violations of this Code will be investigated by HR. Depending on severity, consequences range from a written warning to immediate termination. Employees subject to investigation retain the right to representation and will be informed of the process and outcome.
